**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The TRANSITION rule is satisfied by an existing, detailed exit architecture rather than being absent:

- **Data/records return:** §11.6 (surviving under §12.4) gives either Party an on-request right to destruction of its Confidential Information with written confirmation, subject only to reasonable archival/back-up carve-outs — no immediate-deletion or no-return walk-away.
- **Transition assistance:** §12.3(c)(vi) is an express "Transition Assistance" package (technical assistance, Know-How and prosecution-file transfer, third-party contract assignment, manufacturing tech transfer, clinical trial transfer, commercial transition services agreement, general orderly-transition cooperation), backed by §12.3(c)(iii) sell-off and §12.3(c)(iv)/(d)(iii) transfer of Regulatory Approvals, Regulatory Materials, clinical data and pharmacovigilance databases within fixed windows.
- **Direction:** because Product rights revert to RevMed on termination, most of these duties run from Sanofi to RevMed. That is the bargained reversion consideration, not a rule breach, so we do not flag it. Assistance running to us appears in §12.3(e) (RevMed Change of Control) and §7.2 (RevMed Manufacturing Know-How transfer on Sanofi's request).

Noted in the rationale but not flagged as deviations: all durations and cost allocations are redacted ([***]), so the 90-day/6-month benchmarks cannot be confirmed on the face of the document; and §7.2 is not in the §12.4 survival list, so post-expiry manufacturing know-how support to Sanofi is not expressly preserved — worth confirming in diligence rather than redlining here.
